Jordan: FYI repro for the weird OOM pattern on long KV-cache sessions after we changed allocator knobs earlier today.
Anya: dropping in—what knobs and model?
Jordan: model=redwood-4b, seq_len=4096, batch=3, very KV-heavy. Changed max_split_size_mb 96->384, expandable_segments toggled on, gc_threshold 0.12->0.06.
Jordan: short repro attached inline + perf snapshot. saw repeated small OOMs every ~20 minutes.
Jordan: perf snapshot (trimmed):
```
GPU0: baseline used=10.7GB -> peaks 13.5GB
heap_free_largest=40MB
free_small_pool=2.1GB
alloc_retry_count=7
avg_alloc_split=96MB
fragmentation_delta=+1.2GB over 3h
```
Lee: that largest free of 40MB will block any large contiguous allocs if max_split is >40MB. alloc_retry_count matches.
Mike: do we have kernel selection traces? Bigger allocations usually flip kernel paths.
bench-bot: kernel-distribution from run A (pre-change): small=70%, medium=25%, large=5%
bench-bot: run B (max_split=384): small=50%, medium=30%, large=20%
Jordan: so increasing max_split pushed more "large" kernel choices. When fragmentation prevents an allocation, runtime falls back to expensive split/fallback paths -> latency spikes and occasional OOMs.
Anya: interesting trade: more large kernels gives better throughput when allocations succeed, but increases sensitivity to fragmentation over time.
Lee: KV cache pattern explains accumulation: many pinned small allocations scattered across heap, then occasional transient large attention buffers can't find contiguous space.
Mike: quick experiment notes:
- max_split=96 + expandable_segments=false -> stable, no OOM, but token throughput -6%
- max_split=192 + expandable_segments=true -> intermittent alloc retries but acceptable median latency
- gc_threshold=0.2 -> fewer alloc retries but GC overhead bumps p50 by ~2ms
Jordan: tried a short-run with periodic manual coalescing (triggering GC every 30m) and it cleared fragmentation spikes. Worth automating.
Anya: mitigation proposals:
1) short term: reduce max_split to 128, set gc_threshold=0.18 for long-lived pools
2) mid term: implement attention buffer workspace reuse (reuse ring buffers keyed by max_seq to avoid large transient allocs)
3) long term: allocator improvements to allow large-kernel paths to accept split backing (avoid requiring contiguous free block)
Mike: I'll add heapmap tracing to prod traces to capture heap_free_largest over time and correlate with kernel selection.
Lee: I'll prototype workspace reuse PR (buffer reuse pool per-device). idea: keep N buffers per seq bucket, LRU eviction.
Jordan: can we add a runtime fallback rule: if alloc_fail_count > 1/min revert max_split to safe value automatically?
Anya: Yes. If soak passes on staging we can put an autoswitch in rollout policy.
bench-bot: scheduled nightly soak: staging config id=alloc-soak-202, start=1923458000, duration=24h.
ops-bot: deploy playbook created: https://confluence.internal/alloc/soak-plan-202
Mike: I'll ship heapmap tracing tonight and post results.
Lee: aiming for draft PR with workspace reuse by EOD Fri.
Jordan: I'll run the 24h soak with max_split=128, expandable_segments=true, gc_threshold=0.18 and upload logs. thanks all :thumbsup:
